# Rasterloom 0.1.4 alpha
Work with ChatGPT or Claude directly on your canvas, with editable results and conversations that stay with your project.
## Assistants on the canvas
- Connect your installed ChatGPT or Claude CLI using its existing account sign-in, without entering an API key in Rasterloom. - Press K to place an assistant note for a layer, artboard or canvas. The action is also available in the toolbar and customizable Favorite Actions. - Move notes and chat cards freely, resize the conversation and message field, and choose a beside-pin, canvas or bottom presentation. - Choose a model in the composer. Rasterloom remembers your choice for each provider until you change it. - Each note keeps its own session, messages and draft when you save and reopen the project. - Resolve a note with the checkmark to clear it from the canvas. Search Assistant History to reopen and continue the same conversation. - Read rendered Markdown, copy individual messages, stop a running request and queue a follow-up. Enter sends; Shift-Enter adds a line. - Chat cards become translucent over artwork when they are not targeted. Scroll fades and a Latest action keep longer conversations easy to follow. - Connected assistants can preview the canvas, inspect the targeted layer and use the note's attached position as context.
## More native editing tools for agents
- In-app assistants and external MCP clients share the same native editing tools, including brush, eraser, healing and clone strokes, pixel selections, fills, gradients and filters. - Edit photo and RAW recipes, text, vectors, layer effects, paint stacks, smart objects, masks and design styles. - Remove a photo background into an editable subject mask while preserving the original image and development recipe. - Unlock layers, move linked masks with their artwork and receive clear errors when a layer cannot be edited. - Search and preview the asset library, place original assets, manage collections and use saved versions. - Grant access to a specific folder to browse, preview and import its artwork from a conversation. - Work with PDF text, pages, annotations, links and form fields, and create or arrange moodboards with the same native tools used in the app. - Export artwork, PDFs, moodboards and photo contact sheets. Uninterrupted edits from an assistant turn can be undone together.
## Faster photo development and interface fixes
- Image and RAW development now coalesces live previews while you adjust controls, then refines the result without rendering every intermediate change at full resolution. - Before/after previews stay consistent through cache refreshes and undo, including white balance and curves. - Opening a file no longer brings up an empty Before & After window. - The Artboard tool shortcut is now F. Shift-O still selects the tone tool. - Improved control padding, chat alignment, compact copy buttons and clearer conversation empty states.
Requirements: Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later. Canvas assistants use an installed, signed-in ChatGPT or Claude CLI.

# Rasterloom 0.1.3 alpha
Build out multi-artboard designs faster, with matching backgrounds, direct canvas actions and more reliable connected-agent workflows.
## Artboards on the canvas
- Choose a transparent, white or custom-color background when creating an artboard, just as you can for the first canvas. Solid backgrounds remain editable layers and follow artboard resizing. - With the Artboard tool active, use the + buttons on the top, right, bottom and left edges to create a matching artboard in that position. - Click an artboard's name to select it and activate the Artboard tool. Shift-click names to select multiple artboards. - A shared selection outline encloses all selected artboards. Move them together with their layers; individual artboards keep their resize handles. - Right-click an artboard or its name for Rename / Resize, Duplicate and Delete. Multi-artboard duplication and deletion are each one undoable action. - Delete or Backspace removes selected artboards and their contents. Undo restores the artboards, contents and selection. - Backgrounds, positions and editable content are preserved when saving and reopening projects.
## More reliable MCP workflows
- Layer and tab lists now return structured objects that work correctly with Claude Code and other MCP clients. - Slow or stalled requests no longer block every subsequent call. Agents can still inspect the app while an edit waits for project I/O or rendering. - Requests support cancellation and bounded timeouts. Withdrawn work cannot commit late document changes. - Agent-created canvases start clean, without an empty placeholder layer. - Set text color and tracking when creating text, avoiding an extra recoloring step. - Discover fonts by family and style, with exact PostScript names for text creation and clearer invalid-font errors. - Mesh gradients and device mockup rendering now honor cancelled agent requests before changing the document. - Opened project copies use the source project's name instead of a generic Untitled tab. - Updated tool schemas and the bundled agent guide describe the current result shapes, discovery options and canvas controls.
## A more consistent interface
- Creation sheets, export and document panels, and floating tool panels use Rasterloom's own panel colors, typography and button styling. - Panel appearance follows the app's selected theme, including comparison and PDF workflows.
Requirements: Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.

# Rasterloom 0.1.2 alpha
Develop photos directly on the canvas, preserve their originals, and take them through comparison, print preparation and export.
## Photo editing on the canvas
- A new Develop panel lives in Properties, alongside the existing canvas tools. Its sections open expanded, and adjustments update the canvas live. - Import and develop RAW/DNG files supported by macOS, as well as common photo formats. Original files and editable settings stay together in the project. - Adjust exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites and blacks, with a histogram for reference. - Set white balance using As Shot, Daylight, Cloudy, Shade or Tungsten presets, temperature and tint controls, or an eyedropper that samples a neutral area. - Edit master and individual RGB tone curves directly on a graph. Add, drag and remove control points, enter input/output values, or double-click a point to reset it. - Adjust vibrance and saturation, then refine hue, saturation and luminance for individual color ranges in the color mixer. Advanced controls provide red, green and blue channel balance. - Edits take effect immediately, with no Apply step. Each slider or curve drag is an undoable action, and Reset supports undo too. Switching layers and reopening projects retain their photo settings.
## Before and after
- The sidebar photo preview fills the available width. - Compare the original and edited photo in a larger, resizable window. - Choose a draggable before/after wipe or side-by-side images. Shared zoom and pan keep both views aligned, and Fit returns to the complete image. - Use Before in the Develop panel to inspect the original on the canvas without changing the saved adjustments.
## Faster asset placement
- The asset library preserves original photo data, so placing a library photo retains its Develop controls. - Double-click an asset to place it on the last active canvas. Rasterloom creates a canvas when one is needed. - Right-click asset cards for placement and other asset actions, reducing trips through nested menus.
## Export and print
- Export opens in a larger, resizable panel, with a large encoded preview, transparency checkerboard, and Fit or 100% inspection. - Settings are grouped into image size, file settings, color and precision, metadata, watermarking and print size. JPEG export uses the same full panel. - Export layered compositions directly, with no flattening acceptance checkbox or extra fallback confirmation. - Choose sRGB, Display P3 or Adobe RGB output, with 16-bit PNG/TIFF and output sharpening for photo delivery. - Export HEIC and AVIF when macOS provides the encoder, alongside the existing PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP, PDF, SVG and layered PSD formats. - Control copyright, camera metadata, location metadata and text watermarks. - Check print dimensions and effective photo resolution. Preview a printer/paper ICC profile in the large preview, choose a rendering intent and black-point compensation, and inspect the gamut estimate. - Use a printer ICC profile for TIFF output, or create a PDF photo contact sheet with paper size, grid and caption options.
## Autosave and document versions
- Saved `.rloom` projects update automatically while the document is stable and when Rasterloom moves to the background. Untitled documents keep recovery copies until their first Save. - Document Versions now includes automatic checkpoints alongside named restore points. The latest 20 automatic checkpoints are retained, and named versions remain available. - Restoring a version supports undo. The existing on-disk version is preserved before the first automatic replacement, and changes made by another writer are reported rather than overwritten.
## Better connected-agent workflows
- The app and MCP helper now share an App Group, improving access from Claude Code and other MCP clients. - A live capabilities catalog exposes available operations, filters and adjustments with their parameters, mesh presets, device names, blend modes and export presets. - Agents can discover installed font names and variable-font axes, use fixed-value schemas, and receive errors that identify valid values. - A bundled automation guide is available through MCP and covers both tool workflows and computer-use accessibility identifiers. - Filter search handles punctuation, spaces and case consistently. Filter tiles, search fields, presets and panel actions have stable accessibility identifiers, and floating panels remain accessible while Rasterloom is in the background.
## Interface improvements and fixes
- Tool icons, toolbar menus and other controls have consistent hover feedback and button styling. - Tooltips appear much faster with a brief delay, and hover feedback no longer interrupts their tracking. - Tooltips from inactive workspaces no longer appear over the canvas, and canvas objects no longer show obstructive tooltips. - Improved inspector spacing and control labels prevent awkward wrapping, including in comparison controls. - Moodboards are easier to target from the canvas. - MacBook mockup artwork fills the complete screen beneath the notch.
Requirements: Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.

# Rasterloom 0.1.1 alpha
Create and add artwork without leaving the canvas.
- Generate images with Apple Image Playground on supported Macs. Apple Intelligence must be enabled; availability depends on your macOS version, language and region. Third-party generation providers are not offered. - A new Create panel brings image generation, mesh gradients, device mockups and blank layers together above the canvas. - Search and filter library assets from the canvas, then insert the original artwork as an undoable layer. - Brush and Eraser have separate toolbar icons and favorites, with their existing B and E shortcuts. - Layer actions remain compact icons, separate from creation tools. - Panel headers share aligned divider lines. The selected artwork name stays in Properties. - Resize dividers highlight blue on hover and drag, have a wider hit area, and reset to their default width on double-click.
Requirements: Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.

# Rasterloom 0.1.0 alpha
The first testing release of Rasterloom, a Tiny Things app.
- Layered image editing with retained text, vectors, masks, gradients, retouching, smart artwork and export. - A local asset library and rebuilt moodboards for images, links, notes and colors. - Optional on-device image descriptions and tag suggestions after a separate model download. - Automatic update checks, a manual check, and a quiet update-available button.
Requirements: Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.
